title: A new class of graphs that satisfies the Chen-Chvatal Conjecture -- Conjecture 2.2
_round_note: Round 5. Four proposals; ONE confirmed NEGATIVE result (a FOURTH H5 mechanism barred = frontier advance), THREE refuted (all by their own designated oracle gate). (1) EXECUTED the sole queued H7 experiment (ledger.next_action): a battery of PAIR-INDEXED / shell x shell line-charge functionals over every connected pendant-free diam>=4 graph at n=8 (125) and n=9 (3061). Every GENUINE subset-of-lines pair functional FAILS the >=n gate -- f_far0/periphery/match below-n on 125/125 & ~all 3061 (margins -7/-8), f_far1 -4/-5, closest genuine f_far2 below-n on only 1/125 & 6/3061 (floor -1/-2). The ONLY gate-clearing functional, sum_per_class (per-distance-class distinct-line buckets summed), is PROVEN an OVERCOUNT: sum_per_class > ell on 125/125 (min diff +1), so it double-counts lines shared across distance classes -- exactly the G6/pl empty-counting trap. The H7 pair-indexed / shell-cross-shell charge is REFUTED: no genuine subset-of-lines pair functional reaches n. The H5 barrier now spans a FOURTH mechanism (diametral-pairs, spine G3, pencil/bipencil G5, pair-indexed G8); far/peripheral pairs collapse to few distinct lines (f_match=1 on worst graphs) and the universal line absorbs the diametral ones. Skeptic's hunt found far_ge2 (distinct lines among ALL non-adjacent dist>=2 pairs) is the TIGHTER genuine near-miss (floor -1/0, clears n=9, fails one n=8 graph G?qa`o) -- this and f_far2 are the targets for any future symbolic look. (2) explicit-construction margin-floor M(n) reformulation -- REFUTED by its own n=10 oracle gate: M(8)=1,M(9)=2,M(10)=1 is NON-MONOTONE (predicted M(10)>=2), and the n=10 floor sits at diam=5 (seed I?`bCaWTO), NOT diam=4 (extremal-seed framing mislocated). (3) asymptotic F_far (distinct non-adjacent-pair lines) >=n for n>=9 -- REFUTED: 4 oracle-verified n=10 diam>=4 pendant-free graphs have F_far=9<10 (undershoot count 1->0->4, triggers own KILL signature; decisive witness I?bB@_Wc_ is diam=4 br=0 ell=21, inside the H5 regime). (4) literature-reduction twin-free split -- REFUTED: the twin-free lemma (pendant-free+diam>=4 => twin-free, verified 125/3061/116564) is true but INERT (makes the residual logically identical to H5, zero reduction), and the only non-graveyard citation (Matamala-Villarroel diam-3) is scope-disjoint from diam>=4 ({3}∩{>=4}=∅), reprising the G4 kill. Net: H4/H5 still empirically clean (n<=10, margin floor +1); the EXPLICIT LINE-COUNTING axis for H5 is now exhausted -- four charging mechanisms barred (low- AND high-dimensional), no surviving subset-of-lines functional reaches n. Genuine survivors: a clean true lemma 'pendant-free+diam>=4 => twin-free' (n<=10); near-miss functionals far_ge2/f_far2 (floor -1).
central_question: Conjecture 2.2: there is a FINITE set F_0 of connected graphs such that every connected graph G not in F_0 either has a pendant edge OR satisfies ell(G)+br(G) >= |G|, where ell(G)=number of distinct metric-betweenness LINES, br(G)=number of bridges. Equivalently: the set of BAD graphs -- connected, pendant-edge-free, with ell(G)+br(G) < |G| -- is FINITE. The known route to a DISPROOF (flagged by the paper itself) is to find pendant-free bad graphs that keep appearing without bound; the route to support is to show the bad set stabilises at the explicit F_0 of Figures 1-3.

benchmark.description: The fixed yardstick. Every proposal is scored against the EXACT invariants ell(G), br(G), and the bad-classifier, computed by full BFS metric + networkx. No sampling, no asymptotics.
benchmark.invariants: ell(G) = |{ line(a,b) : a<b }|, line(a,b)={a,b} U {x : [abx] or [axb] or [xab]}, [uvw] iff d(u,v)+d(v,w)=d(u,w) (BFS graph metric); br(G)=#bridges (networkx); pendant edge present iff some vertex has degree 1.
benchmark.bad_predicate: BAD(G) iff G connected AND pendant-edge-free AND ell(G)+br(G) < |G|.

open_crux: Is the set of connected pendant-free BAD graphs (ell+br<n) FINITE, and does it equal the explicit F_0 of Figs 1-3? FRONTIER (Round 5): the problem is split into part (a) brute disproof-witness search and part (b') the structural lemma H5 'pendant-free + diam>=4 => ell(G)>=|G|'. Part (a) is exhausted through n=10 (9,808,209 pendant-free, 0 bad; |bad|=12=|F_0|), with the n=11 full sweep launched but NOT yet completed. Part (b') H5 remains the SOLE live structural lever (H3 bridgeless + H4 diam<=3 + H5 would confine all bad graphs to the bounded regime 'bridgeless, pendant-free, diam<=3, ell<n', a finite-diameter counting problem). THE EXPLICIT SUBSET-OF-LINES LOWER-BOUND AXIS FOR H5 IS NOW EXHAUSTED -- FOUR charging mechanisms barred, spanning BOTH low- and high-dimensional indexing: (i) the naive 'distinct diametral pairs => n lines' heuristic (pairs share lines); (ii) the single-geodesic SPINE charge (G3 -- spine lines line(v0,vi) collapse to the universal line, separator phi identically 0); (iii) the peripheral-PENCIL / bipencil shell-charge (G5 -- F_pencil(v0)<n on 100% of diam>=4 pendant-free n=8,9); (iv) Round 5 -- the explicitly-queued Theta(n^2) PAIR-INDEXED / shell x shell charge (G8 -- every GENUINE pair functional f_far*/f_periphery/f_match is <n, closest f_far2 floor -1/-2; the sole gate-clearing sum_per_class is PROVEN an overcount, >ell on 125/125, the same empty-counting trap that killed pl/G6). The unifying lesson now CLOSES the line-counting axis: low-dimensional base-vertex charges capture only O(diam)=o(n) of ell, while pair/shell-cross-shell charges either (a) collapse -- far/peripheral pairs realize few distinct lines (f_match=1 on worst graphs), the universal line absorbs the diametral ones -- or (b) overcount by re-counting lines shared across classes. No explicit subset-of-lines functional reaches >=n on all diam>=4 pendant-free n<=9 graphs. The two genuine NEAR-MISSES are far_ge2 (distinct lines among all non-adjacent dist>=2 pairs; floor -1/0, clears n=9, fails one n=8 graph G?qa`o) and f_far2 (floor -1/-2) -- candidates for a targeted SYMBOLIC argument, not a counting functional. Side structural facts confirmed n<=10: pendant-free+diam>=4 => twin-free (no equal distance-vectors), but this is INERT for H5 (it is implied on the H5 inputs, removing no difficulty). The empirical n<=10 stability is NOT a proof (empirical_not_proof gate). Plausible next direction given line-counting is exhausted: abandon explicit functionals and attempt a direct structural/induction argument for ell>=n on min-deg-2 diam>=4 graphs (e.g. peeling a far vertex while tracking line-creation), or pivot effort to the H3/H4 direct symbolic attacks.

graveyard.kill_reason: REFUTED (oracle, Round 3): the crux spine-injectivity sub-claim is FALSE on 100% of in-scope graphs -- for every connected pendant-free diam>=4 graph at n=8,9,10 (122750 graphs) and EVERY longest geodesic, the spine lines line(v0,vi) are NOT pairwise distinct and phi is identically 0, because line(v0,vi) generically contains the far endpoint v_d (the [v0 vi x] forward extension swallows the far side), so the separator cannot separate the spine and the lines collapse (often to the universal line). Any H5 proof must charge lines GLOBALLY to BFS shells (see H6), not via a single-geodesic spine.

FRONTIER ADVANCE -- the geodesic half-space / SPINE-charge proof route to H5 is DEAD (G3): an oracle sweep over EVERY connected pendant-free diam>=4 graph at n=8,9,10 (125/3061/116564 = 122750 graphs, 100%) shows that for EVERY longest geodesic the spine lines line(v0,vi) are NOT pairwise distinct and the proposed monotone separator phi(L)=min_x d(x,v_d) is identically 0 (line(v0,vi) generically swallows the far endpoint v_d, collapsing often to the universal line). This bars a SECOND H5 mechanism (after the naive diametral-pairs heuristic) and pins the residual to a GLOBAL BFS-shell line-count (new H6), which must not collapse on the spine-route witnesses. OTHER PROPOSALS: (a) explicit-construction H5 gate over a C4-rich n=11 neighborhood of the 3 tightest diam>=4 seeds -- 614 kept candidates, 0 bad, 0 ell<n; the lone 'deficit=0' graph (J?`bCaWTPC?, n=11, diam=6, ell=11=n, br=0) is is_bad=FALSE and SATISFIES the conjecture (boundary tie, NOT a disproof), so it mildly SUPPORTS H5 at n=11 -- REFUTED as a disproof, kept as supporting evidence. Round 4 (4 proposals; ONE confirmed NEGATIVE = a third H5 mechanism barred = frontier advance; THREE refuted, all variants of dead families). FRONTIER ADVANCE -- executed the sole queued H6 experiment (ledger.next_action) and BARRED the peripheral-PENCIL / bipencil shell-charge as an H5 lower bound (G5). F_pencil(v0)=|{line(v0,w):w}| is a provable subset-of-lines lower bound that CLEARS the ledger's non-collapse bar on both G3 witnesses (f_pencil_min=3 on G?B@vo, 5 on H?ABCp{, NOT the universal line's 1) but FAILS the >=n gate on 100% of diam>=4 pendant-free graphs: pencil_max/min<n on 125/125 (n=8, margin -5) and 3061/3061 (n=9, margin -6/-7); even two-endpoint bipencil<n on 54/125 and 486/3061; the skeptic's strongest variant (best pencil over ALL vertices) reaches >=n on 0/125 and 0/3061. UNIFYING BARRIER (now spanning G3+G5): any functional charging lines to a BOUNDED set of base vertices captures only an O(diam) fraction of ell; the surplus to reach n is GLOBAL-PAIR (Theta(n^2)). Residual H5 mechanism redirected to PAIR-indexed / shell x shell charge (new H7); H6 marked pencil-form-REFUTED. THREE REFUTED proposals: (1) cocktail-party K_{k×2} ell=C(k,2)+1 (oracle k<=14), last bad member k=4 -- REFUTED: duplicates graveyard G1, k<=5 sits inside the exhaustive scan, closed form empirical+overkill (crude ell>=2k suffices), 'unique infinite family' unjustified (K_aa, K_2,2k, Q_d all decay faster). (2) proper-line count pl(G)>=n -- empirically TRUE (min_pl 8/10/10) and non-collapsing, but the proposed per-shell omission-depth quota provably sums to <= #depths <= diam <= n-1 < n (G6): over all 3061 n=9 graphs the 1-line-per-shell sum is <n on 3061/3061, 1351 have a zero-quota shell; pl>=n holds only via an unbounded single bucket -- empty counting engine. (3) Chiniforooshan-Chvatal universal-line split -- the theorem gives Omega(n^{2/7})=o(n) on U=false (cannot reach n; ell>=n there is finite-oracle only) and the U=true split is the identity ell=1+#nontrivial = zero reduction; needs the OPEN de Bruijn-Erdos metric conjecture (circular, like G2); cited arXiv:1011.5341 wrong (QCD paper; correct 0906.0123) (G7). Net: H4/H5 still empirically clean; the low-dimensional charging axis for H5 is now THREE-TIMES barred and the frontier is sharply pinned to a Theta(n^2) pair-indexed charge.

Round 5 (4 proposals; ONE confirmed NEGATIVE = a FOURTH H5 mechanism barred = frontier advance; THREE refuted, EACH by its own designated oracle gate). FRONTIER ADVANCE -- executed the sole queued H7 experiment (ledger.next_action) and BARRED the Theta(n^2) PAIR-INDEXED / shell x shell line charge as an H5 lower bound (G8), CLOSING the explicit subset-of-lines line-counting axis. Over every connected pendant-free diam>=4 graph at n=8 (125) / n=9 (3061): every GENUINE subset-of-lines pair functional fails the >=n gate -- f_far0 below-n 125/3057, f_periphery 122/2970, f_match 125/3061 (margins -7/-8), f_far1 82/1998 (-4/-5), closest genuine f_far2 below-n on 1/125 & 6/3061 (floor -1/-2). The ONLY gate-clearer, sum_per_class (+7/+9), is PROVEN an OVERCOUNT: sum_per_class > ell on 125/125, min diff +1 (double-counts lines shared across distance classes -- the same empty-counting trap that killed pl/G6). Mechanism: far/peripheral pairs collapse to few distinct lines (f_match=1 on worst graphs) and the universal line absorbs the diametral ones, so even Theta(n^2) pair indexing cannot reach n. This is the FOURTH barred H5 line-counting mechanism (diametral-pairs, spine G3, pencil G5, pair-indexed G8) and EXHAUSTS the explicit functional axis -- NO subset-of-lines functional reaches >=n on all diam>=4 pendant-free n<=9 graphs. Genuine survivors: (i) far_ge2 (distinct lines among all non-adjacent dist>=2 pairs), the TIGHTER near-miss with floor -1/0 (clears n=9, fails only G?qa`o at n=8), and f_far2 (floor -1/-2) -- both are SYMBOLIC targets, not new functionals; (ii) a clean structural fact 'pendant-free+diam>=4 => twin-free' (n<=10, recorded as inert H9). Residual H5 route redirected from explicit charges to a STRUCTURAL / INDUCTION (peeling) argument (new H8): the O(1) deficit (near-misses miss n by exactly 1) suggests an ell-recursion that recovers one extra line per peripheral vertex. THREE REFUTED proposals, each killed by its OWN oracle gate: (1) explicit-construction margin-floor M(n) reformulation (G9) -- M(8)=1,M(9)=2,M(10)=1 NON-MONOTONE (predicted M(10)>=2), floor at diam=5 not the claimed unique diam-4 seed G?r@do. (3) literature-reduction twin-free split (G11) -- twin-free lemma true but INERT (residual logically = H5, zero reduction), citation (Matamala-Villarroel diam-3) scope-disjoint from diam>=4, reprises the G4 kill. Net: H4/H5 still empirically clean (n<=10, margin floor +1); the explicit line-counting axis is EXHAUSTED; the frontier is now whether a structural-induction (H8) or a symbolic far_ge2-deficit argument can recover the single missing line. data/scan_n10.json still to be repopulated; scan(n=11) full sweep still pending.

discipline_gates.empirical_not_proof: n<=9 enumeration showing |bad|=12=|F_0| is VERIFICATION, not a proof that F_0 is finite. The bad set could in principle resume at some n>9 (cf. the analogous oriented-triangle-free m(3) sitting between 18 and 25). A finiteness CLAIM stays in live_hypotheses until a symbolic argument (e.g. ell(G)+br(G)>=|G| for all pendant-free G of order > N) is verified.
discipline_gates.audit_not_redteam: Grounding (oracle invariants) and skeptic (searching for a NEW pendant-free bad graph at larger n, or a counterexample to H1/H3) are separate steps, never the same agent call.
discipline_gates.citations_verified: Any external citation (Chen-Chvatal Conjecture, Beaudou-Kahn-Rochet Lemma/Figure numbers, the bridge-to-path disproof of the no-pendant variant) must resolve to the primary source (arXiv:1606.06011) before it carries weight. The F_0 list and Lemma 3.1 numbers used here are from the paper as summarised in the task spec; the line-oracle independently reproduces the Lemma 3.1 ell-values it can build.
